title: Mandatory vaccinations for dogs in Poland
question: What vaccinations are mandatory for dogs in Poland?
short_answer: Rabies vaccination (wścieklizna) is the only legally mandatory vaccine for dogs in Poland. It must be done annually. Other vaccines are strongly recommended.
conditions: Rabies vaccine (szczepienie przeciwko wściekliźnie): mandatory by law from 3 months of age
Must be repeated annually — vet will give you a vaccination book (książeczka zdrowia)
Keep the vaccination booklet — you may need to show it at borders, vets, or shelters
Recommended vaccines: distemper, parvovirus, hepatitis, leptospirosis (DHP + L)
Puppy schedule: first vaccine at 6–8 weeks, boosters at 12 and 16 weeks
Cost: rabies vaccine ~50–80 PLN, full package ~150–250 PLN
exceptions: Dogs travelling to EU countries need a EU Pet Passport and valid rabies vaccination
If you bring a dog from outside the EU: additional requirements apply (blood titre test may be needed)
Unvaccinated dog involved in a bite incident: mandatory 14-day quarantine by law
penalties: No rabies vaccination: fine up to 500 PLN
